entrada.titulo: Enhancing anomaly detection and prevention in Internet of Things (IoT) using deep neural networks and blockchain based cyber security

perfil_anterior.problema: unauthorized access, malware assaults, and data breaches
perfil_anterior.solucao: blockchain-based architecture and integrated DNN to ensure data integrity, enhance anomaly detection, and offer IoT networks autonomous, distributed threat-mitigating properties
perfil_anterior.avaliacao: Showing a 95.25% efficiency in reaction time
perfil_anterior.limites: weaknesses in smart contracts, Sybil attacks, and 51% assaults may still penetrate blockchain-based security procedures

entrada.texto:
Combining input from users’ delay ( [ui − ew′′]), Bayesian-based planning ( Ba [s − t′′]), and an AI-driven 
enrichment mechanism (Ya [enk − ny′′]) into the analysis of response time ( RT ) is what Eq.  23 represents. 
This method keeps cybersecurity threat mitigation very accurate while minimizing system latency.Distributed 
storage alternatives like IPFS or cloud-based systems may be used off-chain to store less sensitive data, reducing 
transaction overhead. The blockchain should only record key security events, including identified abnormalities 
or authentication failures. Further ways to improve performance and decrease blockchain bloat include batching 
transactions and compressing logs. T o minimize delays caused by latency, the system should optimize the 
execution of smart contracts so that automatic answers and real-time verification are possible. Edge computing 
may preprocess IoT data before blockchain integration to further reduce network congestion.
Guaranteeing perfect interaction with the huge IoT systems shown in Fig.  9, the framework ensures a 
94.96% scalability. Unlike centralized security solutions, which struggle with growing network size and data

resposta.resumo: O trecho descreve a integração de armazenamento off‑chain (IPFS ou nuvem) e otimização de contratos inteligentes para reduzir latência, além de usar edge computing para pré‑processar dados IoT. O método mantém alta precisão na mitigação de ameaças, alcançando 94,96% de escalabilidade, e propõe técnicas como batch de transações e compressão de logs para evitar o inchaço da blockchain.
